name: PowerView Trust Enumeration
description: Enumerate domain and forest trusts to map potential lateral movement paths across trust boundaries.

steps.label: Map all trusts across the forest

recommended.note: Escalate from child to parent domain
Abuse forest trust for cross-forest access
Create inter-realm ticket for trust abuse

notes: TrustDirection: Bidirectional=both ways, Inbound=they trust us, Outbound=we trust them. TrustType: External vs Forest matters for SID filtering.

defense.why_it_works: Domain trusts create Kerberos referral paths between domains/forests. Get-DomainTrust/Get-ForestTrust enumerate trust direction, type, and SID filtering status. Bidirectional trusts with SID filtering disabled allow SID History injection - enabling cross-domain/forest DA escalation.
defense.prerequisites: Any domain user. PowerView or AD module. LDAP access (trustedDomain objects readable by all authenticated users).
defense.impact: T1482 Domain Trust Discovery. Maps cross-domain attack paths. Bidirectional forest trust without SID filtering = cross-forest DA escalation via forged PAC with parent SID.
defense.detection:
LDAP query for trustedDomain objects - low signal, hard to distinguish from admin queries. Event 4104 SBL: Get-DomainTrust/Get-ForestTrust. MDI reconnaissance detection.
Adversary uses nltest, PowerShell, or Win32/.NET API to enumerate domain trust relationships (via DSEnumerateDomainTrusts, GetAllTrustRelationships, or LDAP queries), followed by discovery or authentication staging (DET0007/AN0016).
defense.artifacts: Event 4104: Get-DomainTrust / Get-ForestTrust | LDAP query for trustedDomain container | MDI recon alert
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 (ScriptBlockText="*Get-DomainTrust*" OR ScriptBlockText="*Get-ForestTrust*" OR ScriptBlockText="*Get-NetForestTrust*")
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Get-DomainTrust","Get-ForestTrust","Get-NetForestTrust","nltest /domain_trusts")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.prevention:
Enable SID filtering on all external/forest trusts. Audit trust relationships quarterly. Remove unnecessary trusts. MDI deployment.
Audit: Map the trusts within existing domains/forests and keep trust relationships to a minimum.
Network Segmentation: Employ network segmentation for sensitive domains.
defense.evasion: Extremely low signal - single LDAP lookup for trustedDomain objects. No evasion needed.
defense.misconfiguration: Forest trust with SID filtering disabled - allows SID History injection across forest boundary. Bidirectional trust where unidirectional was intended. External trust without quarantine.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Check SID filtering on forest trust:
Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Select Name,TrustType,TrustDirection,SIDFilteringForestAware
# SIDFilteringForestAware = False → SID filtering DISABLED → VULNERABLE

# With SID filtering off, attacker can forge ticket with parent DA SID:
# krbtgt hash + SID history injection = cross-forest DA
defense.secure_config:
# Enable SID filtering on forest trust:
netdom trust ChildDomain.corp.local /domain:corp.local /enablesidhistory:no /filtersids:yes

# Verify:
(Get-ADTrust -Filter {Target -eq 'ChildDomain.corp.local'}).SIDFilteringForestAware  # Should be True

# Quarantine external trusts:
netdom trust ExternalDomain /domain:corp.local /quarantine:yes

# Audit quarterly:
Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Format-Table Name,TrustType,TrustDirection,SIDFilteringForestAware -AutoSize

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.description: Forest trusts (external/forest). See the command syntax for exact parameters and flags.

variations.label: Get-DomainTrustMapping (recursive full trust map)
variations.description: Uses PowerView to enumerate domain trust relationships. Trust direction and type determine whether you can pivot across domain boundaries and which attacks (SID history, TGT forging) apply.

explain:
Enumerates trust relationships to find lateral paths across domain/forest boundaries:
  Get-DomainTrust          list this domain's trusts
  | select SourceName,TargetName,TrustDirection,TrustType   the endpoints, direction, and kind of each trust
Add Get-ForestTrust for forest trusts and Get-DomainTrustMapping to recursively map the whole trust graph - the direction and type tell you which trusts can be abused (e.g. SID History via a parent-child trust).
